Zero per-frame managed (GC) allocations while photo mode is open and idle and while adjusting sliders (after the first-open warmup frame, which builds caches). The idle paths are enforced by allocation gates in the automated test suite on every release run rather than measured once. While closed , the controller only polls the toggle binding. There is no other per-frame work and nothing allocates. Slider value labels use cached lookups and TextMesh Pro's non-allocating numeric SetText .

Measured in the demo scene (Unity 6000.3, mid-range desktop, 640×480 base render in the automated batch run). Informational, not a contract: Supersample Wall time 1× ≈ 60–250 ms 2× ≈ 180–270 ms 4× ≈ 700–880 ms Times scale roughly with output pixel count (a 4× capture of a 1080p view renders at 7680×4320) and are dominated by the GPU readback and PNG encode; expect multiple seconds at 4× from 1080p. A PROCESSING… badge appears automatically during heavy supersampled captures (and never appears in the captured photo).

Repeated open/close cycles are leak-gated in the test suite: zero net scene-object growth and zero Unity-object growth over 100 cycles. The UI prefab is instantiated on each enter and destroyed on exit, so photo mode holds no UI memory while closed; the leak gate above covers the cycle.

Prefer 2× over 4× for social-media-sized output; 4× exists for print-quality shots. Transparent captures render without post-processing (clean alpha), which also makes them slightly cheaper. See Capture for the full capture pipeline.
Quick answers to the questions buyers ask most. For symptom-driven help, see Troubleshooting ; for version migrations, see the Upgrade Guide .

How long does it take to add photo mode to my game? ¶ About 10 minutes. Drag the generated PhotoModePro.prefab into your scene, add your HUD canvases and player root(s) on the PhotoModeController component, and press your toggle key in Play mode. The Quick Start walks through every step. What does the Setup Wizard do? ¶ Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Setup Wizard runs green/yellow/red checks on your project (render pipeline, effects backend, input handling, Cinemachine, TMP Essential Resources and demo materials) and offers one-click fixes for anything yellow or red. Run it first whenever something looks wrong; it catches the most common setup problems (wrong-pipeline demo materials, missing TMP essentials) before they cost you time. Do I need to install any other packages? ¶ No hard dependencies. Recommended/optional: Input System package : recommended; the legacy Input Manager also works with limitations (see below). Post Processing Stack v2 ( com.unity.postprocessing ): only on the Built-in Render Pipeline, for the full adjustment set. Without it the built-in fallback backend is used (exposure, contrast, saturation, vignette, tint, tilt-shift, sharpen, HSL qualifier, LUT filters and transparent capture). TMP Essential Resources : the UI uses TextMeshPro; import them once via Window > TextMeshPro > Import TMP Essential Resources (the Setup Wizard checks this and the demo builder imports them automatically). Can I open photo mode from my own code, e.g. a pause menu? ¶ Yes: using PhotoModePro ; PhotoModeController . Instance . EnterPhotoMode (); PhotoModeController . Instance . ExitPhotoMode (); PhotoModeController . Instance . OnPhotoCaptured += ( path , thumbnail ) => Debug . Log ( $"Saved {path}" ); All lifecycle events also exist as UnityEvents for Inspector-only wiring. See Events and API . Does opening photo mode pause my game? ¶ By default yes: timeScale = 0 with audio paused, and everything restored exactly on exit. A non-pausing "unscaled" mode is available on the settings asset for games that must keep simulating. Audio pausing is controlled separately via PhotoModeSettings.AudioPauseMode ( AudioListenerPause or None for mixer-snapshot-driven games).

Which Unity versions and render pipelines are supported? ¶ Unity 2021.3 LTS or newer , verified on 2021.3, 2022.3 and 6000.3. All three render pipelines: URP (12+) , HDRP (12+) and the Built-in Render Pipeline (full set with Post Processing Stack v2, minimal fallback without it). The right effects backend is detected automatically at runtime. See the Support Matrix and Pipelines . Does it work with both the new Input System and the legacy Input Manager? ¶ Yes. The Input System package is the recommended path and is fully supported. The legacy Input Manager works too, with one documented limitation: gamepad right-stick look and triggers are unavailable, because the default InputManager.asset defines no axes for them and the package never edits your ProjectSettings. Keyboard + mouse is fully supported on legacy. Projects with Active Input Handling set to Both are also verified. Does it work with Cinemachine? ¶ Yes. Photo mode spawns its own free camera (a clone of your main camera) on enter and hands control back on exit, so it doesn't fight Cinemachine: your virtual cameras keep owning the gameplay camera. The Setup Wizard includes a Cinemachine check. See Integrations for details. What about WebGL, mobile and consoles? ¶ Windows / macOS / Linux standalone : fully supported, Mono and IL2CPP (IL2CPP verified with Managed Stripping Level = High). WebGL (v1.1): supported — photos save to the in-game gallery (backed by IndexedDB, persistent across reloads, deletes included) and download on demand via the gallery's Download button: one photo as a PNG, several as one or more zip archives (split into _part1 , _part2 … zips for very large selections). Android (v1.1): supported — touch gestures (one-finger look, pinch zoom, two-finger pan) and a responsive portrait layout; verified in the Android emulator. iOS : expected to work through the same touch path, but untested — no claim made (on the roadmap). Consoles : untested; the gamepad input layer is console-style, but no platform claims are made.

Where are photos saved? ¶ {Application.persistentDataPath}/Photos by default, as timestamped, collision-safe PNGs. Override the folder via PhotoModeSettings.CustomSavePath . In-game, clicking the capture toast (or the save-path row on the CAPTURE tab) opens the folder (on Windows with the new photo selected). See Capture . Why is the Transparent BG toggle missing on HDRP? ¶ HDRP cannot produce clean alpha without an alpha-capable color buffer format on the HDRP asset. That is a project-wide setting the package will not edit, so the capability is honestly reported as unsupported and the toggle is hidden. URP and both Built-in backends support transparent capture; transparent frames render without post-processing so the alpha stays clean. See Pipelines . How large can captures be? ¶ 1x, 2x or 4x supersampled. A 4x capture of a 1080p view renders at 7680×4320. Heavy supersampled captures show a "PROCESSING…" badge automatically while the blocking render runs. See Performance for measured wall-times. Does photo mode allocate GC garbage every frame? ¶ No. Photo mode does zero per-frame managed (GC) allocations while open and idle and while adjusting sliders, after the first-open warmup frame that builds caches. While closed, the controller only polls the toggle binding. The idle paths are enforced by allocation gates in the release test suite. See Performance .

Can I rebind the keys? ¶ Yes. The toggle, hide-UI and capture hotkeys (and pause behavior, camera limits, save folder and more) live on the PhotoModeSettings asset. Duplicate it or create one via Assets > Create > Photo Mode Pro > Settings . When you change a hotkey in the Inspector, an editor dialog offers to update the matching on-screen hint chips for you. Can I restyle the UI to match my game? ¶ Yes. The whole UI restyles from a single PhotoModeUITheme asset: colors, fonts, sprites, motion (hover/press scales, transition durations) and UI audio (hover/click/shutter sounds). See Theming . Is the UI fully gamepad-navigable? ¶ Yes. D-pad navigates, sticks stay reserved for the camera (AAA split scheme). The first control of the active tab is selected the moment photo mode opens, and navigation can never go dead: pressing a navigation input while nothing is selected re-selects the first control automatically.

Why does the demo render pink/magenta? ¶ The demo materials were generated for a different render pipeline than the one your project is using. Since 1.0.0 the demo is pipeline-aware: opening the demo scene under a mismatched pipeline offers "Rebuild demo for current pipeline" . Accept it, or run Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Build Demo Assets manually. See Troubleshooting . Can I delete the Demo folder? ¶ Yes, it is safe to delete. Everything demo-related (scene, third-party art and audio, and the demo builders) lives under Assets/PhotoModePro/Demo/ , and nothing outside it references that folder. One thing to know: the generated controller/UI prefabs, settings, theme and presets live under Demo/Generated/ , so if you delete the demo, create your own settings asset ( Assets > Create > Photo Mode Pro > Settings ) and add the PhotoModeController component to a GameObject directly. Who made the demo art, and can I ship it? ¶ All bundled third-party demo assets are CC0 (public domain) , from Quaternius, Kenney, Poly Haven, ambientCG and OpenGameArt, with full provenance in Demo/ThirdParty/ATTRIBUTIONS.md . You may use them, but remember: the product you bought is the photo mode system ; the demo art exists to show it off, and the same CC0 assets are freely available from their original sources. A Welcome window appeared after import — will it keep popping up? ¶ No. It shows once per machine on first import (gated by an EditorPrefs flag) and is never re-shown, including across updates. You can reopen it any time via Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Welcome . How do I get support? ¶ Use Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Report a Bug , or email support.dan.max@gmail.com . Before reporting, run Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Run Self-Test and attach the generated PhotoModeSelfTest.json ; it captures the environment details we need. See also Troubleshooting .

Symptom-driven fixes, including every historical bug fixed in 0.8.x–1.0.0. First steps for almost anything: update to the latest version, run Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Setup Wizard (one-click fixes for pipeline, input, TMP and demo-material problems), and run Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Run Self-Test . Version check Many entries below were bugs fixed in a specific release. The current version is listed in the Changelog ; if you are behind, updating is usually the whole fix.

Symptom: The demo scene (or its props) shows pink/magenta materials. Cause: The demo materials were generated for a different render pipeline than the one currently active — pink is Unity's "shader not supported" color. Fix: Since 1.0.0 the demo is pipeline-aware: materials are generated for the active pipeline, and opening the demo scene under a mismatched pipeline offers "Rebuild demo for current pipeline" (your choice can be persisted with don't-ask-again). Accept it, or run Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Build Demo Assets manually. On 0.9.0 and earlier the demo was URP-only; update the package. The Setup Wizard's demo-materials check flags this too.

t: TextMeshPro text is missing or shows boxes
b: Symptom: UI labels are invisible or render as empty squares. Cause: The TMP Essential Resources are not imported in your project. The photo mode UI uses TextMeshPro. Fix: Import them once via Window > TextMeshPro > Import TMP Essential Resources , or use the Setup Wizard's one-click fix (it checks TMP essentials). The demo builder imports them automatically.

Symptom: You worry the UI needs an EventSystem your scene doesn't have (or, on old versions, the panel didn't respond to input without one). Cause: UGUI input requires an EventSystem; not every game scene has one. Fix: Fixed in 0.9.0; update the package. Photo mode now creates an EventSystem on open if the scene has none (matching your active input handling), logs a single info message, and removes it on exit. The scene is left exactly as it was found. If you prefer, add your own EventSystem and photo mode will use it.

t: Photo mode opens but the game keeps running
b: Symptom: Entering photo mode doesn't freeze gameplay. Cause: The pause behavior on your PhotoModeSettings asset is set to the non-pausing "unscaled" mode. Or your gameplay code runs on unscaled time, so timeScale = 0 doesn't affect it. Fix: Check the pause behavior on the settings asset assigned to your PhotoModeController (the default pauses via timeScale = 0 ). If your game loop uses unscaled time deliberately, gate it yourself from the controller's OnEntered / OnExited events; see Events and API .

t: Audio doesn't resume (or doesn't pause) after photo mode
b: Symptom: Game audio stays paused after exiting photo mode, or never pauses on enter, typically in games that drive audio through mixer snapshots. Cause: PhotoModeSettings.AudioPauseMode controls this. The default, AudioListenerPause , sets AudioListener.pause on enter and restores the prior value exactly on exit; if your own code also writes AudioListener.pause , or your audio runs through snapshot transitions, the two systems fight. Fix: Set AudioPauseMode to None (the package then never touches audio) and transition your own snapshots from the events: controller . OnEntered += () => pausedSnapshot . TransitionTo ( 0.1f ); controller . OnExited += () => gameplaySnapshot . TransitionTo ( 0.1f ); Upgrading from 0.8.x AudioPauseMode replaced the old pauseAudio bool in 0.9.0. Projects that had unchecked pauseAudio must select None once on their settings asset; see the Upgrade Guide .

t: Gamepad navigation goes dead after a mouse click
b: Symptom: Arrow keys / D-pad do nothing when photo mode opens, or stop working after clicking a control with the mouse, until you switch tabs with Q/E. Cause: Mouse clicks clear the EventSystem selection by design (so the focus ring never lingers for mouse users); older versions had no recovery path, so navigation lost its anchor. Fix: Fixed in 0.9.0. Update the package. The first control of the active tab is auto-selected on open, and pressing a navigation input while nothing is selected re-selects it, so navigation never goes dead. If it persists: call PhotoModeUIController.EnsureSelection() from your own code, and report it via Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Report a Bug .

t: Gamepad right stick or triggers don't work
b: Symptom: Right-stick look and trigger fly up/down do nothing on gamepad. Cause: You are on the legacy Input Manager. The default InputManager.asset defines no axes for the right stick or triggers, and the package never edits ProjectSettings. This is a documented limitation rather than a bug. Fix: Install and enable the Input System package (recommended), or add the missing axes to your own InputManager.asset . Keyboard + mouse is fully supported on legacy.

t: Focus rings are cut off at panel edges
b: Symptom: The thin focus ring around toggles, preset buttons, Fly/Orbit, 1x/2x/4x or the capture-folder row is clipped by the side panel's scroll mask. Cause: Focus rings extend a few pixels beyond each control; without enough inner content padding the scroll viewport's mask clips them. The 1.0.0 regression had a subtler cause: the hover/selection scale-up (theme HoverScale ) pushed rings on full-width controls past the original padding. Fix: Fixed in 0.9.0 and finally in 1.0.0 (padding is now computed from the ring size and the theme's selection scale, and regeneration-proof regression tests guard it). Update the package. If it persists: you are likely using a custom theme with a large HoverScale ; reduce it, or rebuild the UI prefab via Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Build Demo Assets .

t: Keyboard/gamepad selection scrolls out of view
b: Symptom: Arrowing down a long tab (e.g. Effects) moves the selection below the visible scroll area and the panel doesn't follow. Cause: Older versions had no scroll-follow logic for EventSystem selection changes. Fix: Fixed in 0.9.0; update the package. The panel now auto-scrolls minimally, just enough to reveal the selected control plus its focus ring. It never moves when the selection is already visible.

t: The highlight overlaps neighboring controls or hides toggle checkmarks
b: Symptom: A soft blue glow bleeds past controls, overlaps the bottom menu / presets / 1x-2x-4x row, lingers after mouse clicks, hides toggle checkmarks, or sits on the wrong supersample button. (Phase 2 items 2–5, 13, 27) Cause: The original expanding soft-glow highlight extended 8–12 px past controls and persisted after clicks. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1. Update the package. The glow was replaced by a thin ~2 px snug outline ring (circular on knobs/toggles, rounded-rect on buttons/tabs) that appears only during keyboard/gamepad navigation; mouse clicks clear the selection.

t: The Effects panel overflows / mouse wheel zooms instead of scrolling
b: Symptom: Long tabs run off the panel with no way to scroll, and the mouse wheel zooms the camera even when the pointer is over the UI. (Phase 2 items 1, 9) Cause: Pre-0.8.1 the side-panel pages had no scroll view and wheel input went to camera zoom unconditionally. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1. Update the package. All pages live in a shared ScrollRect with a slim scrollbar; the wheel scrolls the panel when the pointer is over any UI and zooms the camera otherwise. Wheel zoom also updates the FOV slider live (two-way sync).

t: The aperture slider seems to do nothing above f/3
b: Symptom: Dragging the aperture slider up changes bokeh only at the low end; most of the travel produces no visible difference. Cause: The old slider range extended far past visually useful f-stops, mapped linearly, so almost all the travel sat in a perceptual dead zone. Fix: Fixed in 1.0.0. Update the package. The slider is re-ranged to f/0.7–f/16 with a perceptual log-stop mapping, so the full travel produces visible depth-of-field change. Out-of-range values from old presets or scripts clamp when applied (no API break; the property still accepts any positive value). See the Upgrade Guide .

t: The Focus Dist slider seems to do nothing above ~3 m
b: Symptom: Focus distance visibly pulls only at the low end of the slider. (Phase 2 item 15) Cause: The slider mapped 0.1–100 m linearly; the visibly focus-pulling 0.1–3 m range occupied a sliver of the travel. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1; update the package. The slider now uses a logarithmic mapping (half the travel covers 0.1–3 m); the readout stays in real meters.

t: Focus Dist and Aperture rows show while Depth of Field is off
b: Symptom: The DoF sub-controls remain visible with the DoF toggle off. (Phase 2 item 16) Cause: A UI bug. The rendered blur deactivated correctly, but the rows did not hide. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1. Update the package.

t: Slider changes don't show in HDRP
b: Symptom: On HDRP, the Focus Dist and Aperture sliders have no effect. (Phase 2 items 37, 38) Cause: FOV smoothing wrote Camera.fieldOfView every frame, which silently resets usePhysicalProperties , so HDRP's physical-camera depth of field never saw the values. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1. Update the package. The camera is now driven via focalLength while physical properties are in use. If a custom camera script of yours writes fieldOfView on the photo camera every frame, it will reintroduce the problem; drive focalLength instead on physical cameras.

t: Film grain or vignette looks different across pipelines
b: Symptom: The same slider value reads much stronger or weaker on one pipeline (originally: grain far stronger on PPv2 than URP, vignette far weaker on PPv2 than URP). (Phase 2 items 30, 31) Cause: The underlying post stacks respond differently to identical parameter values. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1. Update the package. URP grain uses a coarse lookup with low luminance response to match the PPv2 look, and PPv2 vignette response is boosted toward URP's. Subtle character differences remain by nature of the stacks; see Pipelines .

t: Effect controls are missing on the Built-in pipeline
b: Symptom: Temperature, film grain and depth of field don't appear in the UI on Built-in. Cause: com.unity.postprocessing (Post Processing Stack v2) is not installed, so the built-in fallback backend is active. It supports exposure, contrast, saturation, vignette, tint, tilt-shift, sharpen, the HSL qualifier, LUT filters and transparent capture; unsupported controls (temperature, film grain, depth of field and the rest) hide automatically. Fix: Install Post Processing Stack v2 for the full adjustment set. The Setup Wizard's effects-backend check points this out. See Pipelines for the capability matrix.

t: The Transparent BG toggle is missing on HDRP
b: Symptom: No transparent-capture option appears on HDRP. Cause: By design. Clean alpha would require an alpha-capable color buffer format on the HDRP asset, which the package does not edit; the capability is reported as unsupported and the toggle hides. Fix: None on HDRP. URP and both Built-in backends support transparent capture. See the FAQ and Pipelines .

t: Captured PNG has UI in it
b: Symptom: Your game's HUD appears in captured photos. Cause: Photo mode hides only the canvases listed in the controller's Game Ui Canvases field; a HUD canvas not listed there (especially world-space or camera-space canvases the photo camera can see) renders into the shot. Fix: Add your HUD canvases to Game Ui Canvases on the PhotoModeController ; they are hidden on enter and restored exactly on exit. See Capture .

t: Capture flash and thumbnail don't appear with the UI hidden
b: Symptom: With Hide UI active, capturing works but you get no white flash, shutter feedback or thumbnail toast. (Phase 2 item 39) Cause: Pre-0.8.1, Hide UI disabled the whole root canvas and took the capture feedback down with it. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1. Update the package. Capture feedback (flash, shutter sound, toast) is now exempt from Hide UI on every pipeline; only the chrome (toolbar, panel, hint bar) hides.

t: Capturing at 4x freezes the game with no feedback
b: Symptom: A 4x capture blocks for seconds and nothing indicates progress. (Phase 2 item 10) Cause: Supersampled captures render synchronously on the main thread; older versions showed nothing during the block. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1. Update the package. 2x/4x captures now show a static "Processing…" badge for the duration (it never appears in the photo). The wall-time itself is expected — a 4x capture of a 1080p view renders at 7680×4320; see Performance .

t: Photo mode won't exit right after pressing capture
b: Symptom: Pressing the toggle immediately after capturing does nothing for a moment. Cause: By design: ExitPhotoMode() no-ops while a capture's async GPU readback is in flight (a few frames), to avoid tearing down the photo camera mid-readback. Fix: Wait the fraction of a second; the exit then proceeds normally.

t: Captures look slightly different from the on-screen image
b: Symptom: A capture is crisper than the live view, or you expected TAA in the shot. Cause: By design. Temporal anti-aliasing (URP and HDRP) is disabled for the duration of every capture and dynamic resolution is forced off, because TAA history is invalid for an offscreen render and produces ghosting/jitter. MSAA/SMAA/FXAA are unaffected. Fix: Nothing to fix. This guarantees artifact-free output at exactly the requested size.

t: Player pops or jumps after Hide Player
b: Symptom: Toggle Hide Player on and off, exit photo mode, and the character jumps or pops on return to gameplay. Cause: Older versions hid the player with SetActive(false/true) ; re-activation reset CharacterController grounding and rebound the Animator. Additionally, a shared binding (e.g. Space as both fly-up and jump) could bleed into gameplay on the closing frame. Fix: Fixed in 0.9.0. Update the package. Hide Player now disables only the player's Renderer components, so physics/animation state survives exactly (regression-tested for position/velocity/grounded equality). If your gameplay code shares bindings with photo mode, also adopt the documented exit-frame pattern: var photoMode = PhotoModeController . Instance ; if ( photoMode != null && ( photoMode . IsActive || photoMode . ExitedThisFrame )) return ; // photo mode owns input this frame

t: The demo character shrinks or scales up during jumps
b: Symptom: The demo adventurer briefly becomes tiny then scales back up while jumping, or after Hide Player. (Phase 2 items 20, 22) Cause: Imported animation clips keyed m_LocalScale , which snapped the model back to FBX units during the airborne state and on Animator rebind. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1; update the package. The animator now uses de-scaled copies of the clips. If it persists after updating, run Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Build Demo Assets to regenerate the demo.

t: Hint chips overlap my game's UI (or look stacked/cramped)
b: Symptom: The hotkey hint chips collide with other UI, or pile up as a tall stack in the bottom-left corner. Earlier: the chips were too small to read. Cause: The chips were originally undersized (fixed in 0.9.0 with a ×1.5 scale-up into four short rows), and the 0.9.0 four-row block read as a cramped stack at some window sizes. Fix: Fixed in 1.0.0; update the package. The chips now form a single row along the bottom screen edge (wrapping to a second row only on very narrow/portrait windows) and the toolbar is raised so the two can never intersect; verified at 16:9, 21:9 and 4:3. If your own HUD occupies the bottom edge during photo mode, add its canvas to Game Ui Canvases so it hides while photo mode is open.

t: Hint chips show the wrong keys after rebinding
b: Symptom: You changed hotkeys on the settings asset but the on-screen hints still show the old keys. (Phase 2 item 12) Cause: Pre-0.8.1, hint text was not updated on hotkey changes. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1. Update the package. Changing a hotkey in the Inspector now offers (via an editor dialog) to update the matching hint chips in the UI prefab. If you declined the dialog or use a moved/duplicated prefab, change the key again to re-trigger it, or edit the chip labels on your prefab copy.

t: The NONE preset button is missing
b: Symptom: The Presets tab no longer has a NONE entry. Cause: By design since 0.9.0: NONE was visually indistinguishable from Clean , so it was removed. Clean is now the first preset and the active default. Fix: Nothing to fix. ApplyPreset(null) remains the programmatic reset and maps to the same state, with no API break. See Presets .

t: Clicking the capture toast does nothing
b: Symptom: The thumbnail toast after a capture isn't clickable. (Phase 2 item 6) Cause: Pre-0.8.1, the toast blocked no raycasts. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1. Update the package. Clicking the toast opens the file browser with the new photo selected (Explorer reveal on Windows; folder open elsewhere). The save-path row on the CAPTURE tab is clickable too.

t: The FOV slider ignores my Min/Max FOV settings
b: Symptom: PhotoModeSettings.MinFov/MaxFov limit wheel zoom but the FOV slider still runs 10–120. (Phase 2 item 14) Cause: Pre-0.8.1, the slider range was hardcoded. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1. Update the package. The slider range is read from the settings asset at UI bind time.

t: Sprint doesn't speed up camera roll
b: Symptom: Holding Shift speeds up movement but Z/C roll stays slow. (Phase 2 item 8) Cause: Pre-0.8.1, the sprint multiplier applied to movement only. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1; update the package. Roll now uses the same SprintMultiplier . (0.8.1 also added the missing "Space/Ctrl · Up/Down" and "Z/C · Roll" hint chips, Phase 2 item 7.)

t: Hint text is hard to read over bright surfaces
b: Symptom: Floating hint labels, toolbar Q/E hints or the toast filename wash out over white/bright backgrounds; the demo HUD looked like plain text. (Phase 2 items 21, 25) Cause: Scene-floating text had no outline, and the old demo HUD was a single legacy Text element. Fix: Fixed in 0.8.1. Update the package. Scene-floating text now gets a thin black TMP outline + underlay, and the demo HUD is rebuilt from the photo-mode UI building blocks.

t: I can't find a camera collision toggle in the UI
b: Symptom: Camera collision can't be switched in-game. Cause: By design. Collision is a settings-asset-only option ( Enable Collision on PhotoModeSettings ) with no in-game toggle. Fix: Set it on the settings asset. See Camera .

t: My forced backend override is ignored
b: Symptom: You set PhotoModeSettings.BackendOverride but a different backend runs, with a warning in the console. Cause: The forced backend is unavailable in the project (e.g. forcing Hdrp in a URP project, or PostProcessingV2 without the package installed). An unavailable forced backend logs one warning and falls back to Auto. Fix: Install/activate the matching pipeline or package, or leave the override on Auto; detection from the active render pipeline asset is reliable. See Pipelines .

t: The Profiler shows GC allocations while photo mode is open
b: Symptom: With the Profiler attached in the editor, sliders or idle photo mode appear to allocate a little every frame, despite the zero-GC claim. Cause: Editor-only instrumentation. Probes show the bytes come from uGUI/TMP editor profiler markers and the measuring recorder itself: uGUI's Slider.Set alone allocates ~123 B/frame in editor play mode with no package code involved. The package's own pipeline (model write, backend apply, label SetText ) allocates zero bytes above idle; the release test suite's allocation gates assert the idle paths. Fix: Profile a player build; the editor-only allocations vanish. Expect one warmup allocation on the first open (cache building), then zero per-frame GC. See Performance .

Run Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Run Self-Test . It writes PhotoModeSelfTest.json with your environment and check results. Use Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Report a Bug (or email support.dan.max@gmail.com ) and attach PhotoModeSelfTest.json , plus your Unity version, render pipeline and reproduction steps. The FAQ covers intentional behaviors that are sometimes mistaken for bugs, and the Support Matrix lists exactly what is verified where.
All notable changes to Photo Mode Pro are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog .

Fixed ¶ Captures now keep the game's MSAA level at supersample 1, flatten alpha on opaque PNGs (no more holes where particles or post effects wrote transparency), and apply the color extras (LUT filter, HSL qualifier) to transparent-background shots. The demo scenes no longer serialize references to the Input System package's default actions or URP's sprite material: the event system module is now added at runtime to match the project's input handling, and the 2D demo uses a generated pipeline-appropriate sprite material, so the demos import clean on legacy-input, Built-in and HDRP projects. Physical-camera state survives captures and studio bookmarks: field-of-view writes route through focal length while the physical model is on, so HDRP physical depth of field no longer silently decouples after one snap. Hotkeys stand down while a text field is focused, arrow keys no longer fly the camera on the legacy input backend while navigating the panel, and an invisible game menu can no longer be driven from inside photo mode. Values set from script before the first frame (supersample, transparent capture) are no longer clobbered by the settings defaults, a throwing event subscriber no longer breaks the capture flow, and the tiled film grain now matches the preview's strength. Gallery robustness and speed: tab switches and deletes reuse cached sidecar metadata instead of rescanning the whole folder, the fullscreen viewer loads photos without freezing input, failed deletes and favorite writes surface in the status line, and photos without camera data show NO CAMERA DATA instead of teleporting the camera to the world origin. WebGL: custom save paths outside the persistent mount are refused with a warning instead of silently losing photos, multi-part downloads ride one click per part so browsers cannot swallow them, and failed IndexedDB flushes are reported. Shared-file hardening: look files, sidecars and .cube imports are size-capped and reject non-finite values, and sidecar/look writes are atomic so a crash cannot corrupt them. See issues.csv ids 393-507 for the full list of 115 issues found and fixed in this pass.

Fixed ¶ The package compiles again on Unity 2021.3 and 2022.1 with HDRP 12/13: the physical camera now routes aperture, shutter speed, ISO and blade count through HDAdditionalCameraData.physicalParameters on those versions instead of Camera members that only exist from 2022.2. A failed capture is no longer silent: the toast now reports CAPTURE FAILED with the reason for both normal and tiled captures instead of only logging to the console. Interrupting a capture mid-readback (closing photo mode, a scene change) no longer leaks the full-resolution readback texture and render target. Closing and reopening photo mode in the same frame no longer leaves the new session without a working EventSystem; UI teardown now runs synchronously on exit. A thumbnail or sidecar failure after a tiled capture finished writing no longer reports the whole capture as failed and orphans the file. On Built-in with Post Processing v2, temporal anti-aliasing is paused for the shot the way it already was on URP and HDRP, removing ghosting from supersampled captures and seams from tiled ones. Tiled captures suppress scene volume effects even when the camera's Volume Mask excludes the Default layer, and scene depth of field no longer bands at tile seams when photo-mode depth of field is off. URP cameras using a non-default renderer (custom features, 2D Renderer) keep that renderer in the photo-mode preview and in captures. Activating overlays or extras no longer drops MSAA on URP: the presenter now reads the sample count from the pipeline asset instead of the quality setting URP ignores. Capture Studio renders now step-halve supersampled shots (no more residual shimmer), apply the active LUT filter, render letterboxed cameras at full frame, and report when a transparent background is not supported on the current pipeline instead of silently writing an opaque PNG. Deleting a saved look now uses the same press-again-to-confirm flow as every other destructive button, and IMPORT LUTS / EXPORT .CUBE show their results in the panel instead of only in the console. Exported .cube files get a unique name instead of silently overwriting an export made in the same second. The photo gallery disables its pager buttons at the first and last page, supports UI prefabs with a custom thumbnail slot count without hiding photos, and reports WebGL download failures on screen. A right-mouse drag that starts on the panel no longer rotates the camera and grabs the cursor, matching how touch drags already behaved. Dragging a light marker no longer drops the drag when the camera moves behind the light. The quick start guide's per-pipeline table now covers all 18 adjustments, the offline PDF is rebuilt from the corrected docs, and the docs landing page describes the current feature set.

Fixed ¶ A failure while photo mode opens (a throwing custom UI prefab, an effects backend that cannot initialize) no longer wedges the game at timeScale 0 with the main camera disabled: the enter sequence now rolls back everything it committed and logs the cause. Re-entering photo mode restores session-sticky extras: the LUT filter, tilt-shift, sharpen, HSL qualifier and the histogram/peaking/zebra overlays now apply on the first frame instead of waiting for a slider touch. Closing photo mode no longer overwrites a timeScale or audio pause the game itself set while the session was open (an expiring slow-mo timer, a pause on focus loss); photo mode only restores values it still owns. Layer exports and the capture sidecar use the camera pose from the moment the shutter fired, so flicking the mouse right after a shot can no longer produce depth/normal/ID files that do not line up with the beauty photo. URP and HDRP projects whose camera Volume Mask excludes the Default layer get photo effects again: the session volume now follows the photo camera's mask (exposure, contrast, depth of field, bloom and curves were silently dead in such projects). Exported .cube LUTs match the preview in more projects: the bake pins scene auto-exposure for its one render and copies the game camera's volume mask and trigger onto the bake camera, so dedicated-layer grades are included. Depth, normal and ID/matte layers cut out URP alpha-tested materials at the authored cutoff instead of the square of it, so foliage and hair silhouettes match the beauty photo. Legacy Animation components freeze during Unscaled-pause photo sessions like everything else (rotating pickups and windmill props no longer drift between the photo and its layer exports). Gamepad and keyboard navigation can no longer die after closing the fullscreen viewer or confirming a delete: focus stranded on a deactivated control is detected and reseated. The gallery fills thumbnails a couple per frame instead of decoding every photo on the page synchronously, so browsing pages of 4K captures no longer freezes the UI for seconds; transient decode failures also retry on the next gallery refresh instead of leaving blank tiles all session. Shared .look.json files are validated on load: non-finite or out-of-range values are clamped to their documented ranges, names render inert instead of as rich-text markup, and re-saving a renamed look no longer resurrects it after a delete. The legacy input backend survives projects whose default InputManager axes were renamed or removed (one warning instead of an exception every frame), and gamepad sticks ease in smoothly from the deadzone edge instead of jumping to 15 percent deflection. The physical camera's shutter time now actually drives the motion-blur adjustment as documented. A full disk during a capture no longer litters the Photos folder with up to a thousand zero-byte PNGs while retrying name collisions, and looks or presets named after Windows reserved device names (CON, AUX, COM1) save correctly. Scene dim handles more scenes correctly: the rendered skybox dims with the world (a sunset HDRI no longer floats at full brightness over a blacked-out scene), buyer edits made through TrackSceneLight survive slider moves, baked-only lights produce a clear one-time warning instead of a slider that looks broken, rig lights on Built-in raise the pixel-light budget for the session so they keep shadows, and the early-restore API also restores ambient and backgrounds. HDRP rig spot lights get their 60 percent flat core on Unity 2021/2022 (innerSpotPercent was left at its default of zero there). The relight rig root now lives in the photo session's scene, so unloading a streamed chunk mid-session no longer destroys the rig lights while the UI still lists them. Capture Studio: bookmarks in orthographic (2D) projects record and restore the zoom level, renders apply the same TAA bracket as runtime captures, per-project window state uses a stable key (the old…

Fixed ¶ Gallery "go to shot" reproduces physical-lens photos exactly: the saved FOV is applied through the lens path instead of being clamped into the roam range (a 200 mm shot no longer reopens at 10°), HDRP physical depth of field survives the teleport, and 2D photos restore their exact recorded zoom via a new orthographic-size field in the sidecar. The mouse wheel no longer destroys the physical camera's framing while the lens model is enabled, and photo mode opens with the game camera's roll (Dutch angles are preserved instead of snapping level). Camera collision now applies in Orbit mode too (swinging or dollying could push the camera through walls). URP games with a custom Volume Mask keep their grade in photo mode: the photo camera clones volumeLayerMask/volumeTrigger like the HDRP path, and HDRP cameras with physical lens shift open correctly framed. A crash inside a capture (out-of-memory on huge supersamples, device removed) can no longer wedge photo mode at timeScale 0 with capture state stuck; both capture routines contain failures and reset cleanly. Object-ID layer PNGs match their _id_map.json colors in linear color-space projects; layer exports respect the photo camera's culling mask, cut out alpha-tested foliage instead of exporting solid quads, and render with the same TAA/dynamic-resolution/viewport bracket as the beauty pass. Tiled captures: a user-forced camera aspect survives the capture, failures restore all overridden state, file naming is race-safe between instances, the sidecar no longer claims a supersample factor, and the toast thumbnail shows the output's framing on ultrawide screens. Exported .cube LUTs are clean color transforms: bloom/CA/distortion/motion blur no longer bake spatial artifacts into the grid, the HSL qualifier and active LUT filter are included, and the bake honors a forced backend. Exiting photo mode leaves idle cutscene directors alone (their actors no longer snap to the timeline's start pose), and particle systems freeze during Unscaled-pause sessions like everything else. HDRP rig spot lights match URP/Built-in brightness (the lumen conversion assumed a reflector that was never enabled), and HDRP film grain uses the same response curve as URP for slider parity. The package compiles again on Unity 2021.3.0–17 (three subsystems used an API introduced in 2021.3.18). Gallery: reloaded thumbnails of supersampled photos no longer shimmer, 32K photos open in the viewer (reduced preview instead of a decode failure), the modal viewer traps gamepad focus, closing it releases the photo's memory, page flips clear selection and armed delete confirms, and WebGL "download all" chunks its archives instead of risking an out-of-memory. Overlay toggles (histogram/peaking/zebras) stay in sync across sessions; free-placed lights no longer snap when the Distance slider is touched; a light marker dragged to the screen edge keeps its grip; touch scrolling can't trigger accidental multi-select holds; and legacy-input projects get working gamepad UI navigation and cancel. Capture Studio: scene-dim Undo covers ambient light state, dropped-feature warnings surface on successful renders, versions resolve under UPM cache installs, custom-SRP projects get honest wizard rows, deleting a rig light keeps the right selection, and headless CI runs always write their JSON result. Demo: rotated props lose their phantom collider margins, touch devices get a PHOTO button, the viewer bar and HUD hints fit narrow screens, hint chips honor a rebound toggle key, and the WebGL demo re-locks the cursor after the browser releases pointer lock.

Fixed ¶ An undeclared GameUiTag/PlayerTag no longer wedges the game mid-enter (paused, camera off): the tag lookup warns and hides nothing instead. Gallery "go to shot" now lands exactly on the saved pose in Orbit mode (teleport switches to Fly so the orbit solver can't drag the camera off). Orthographic (2D) cameras get a correct tiled 8K/16K/32K capture; the tiled path previously always built a perspective frustum. Tiled capture restores custom camera projections (oblique near planes, jitter) instead of discarding them, deletes the partial PNG a failed run used to leave in the gallery, and no longer bands lens distortion, bloom, chromatic aberration or motion blur at seams on PPv2/Built-in. HDRP AOV layer exports release their GPU buffers (one full-resolution buffer leaked per layer per capture). Runtime supersample is clamped to the GPU texture limit (4× on 5K/8K displays produced failed captures). Cycling the gallery sort while multi-selecting can no longer retarget the ticks at different photos before a delete; sorting now exits selection mode. Hiding the UI while the fullscreen photo viewer was open no longer loses the toolbar for the rest of the session. The capture flash shows with reduce-motion themes; the keyboard/gamepad focus ring and click sounds also survive reduce-motion now. Saved looks no longer overwrite an existing "Look N" file after deleting a non-last look; a free name is picked. Imported .cube/PNG LUT strips and saved looks are bilinear-filtered like the built-in filters (red/green banding fixed), and focus peaking compares raw pixels so LUTs/tilt-shift can't flood the overlay. Scene Dim no longer scales camera-background alpha (semi-transparent skies in alpha-preserving captures), and an early scene-light restore no longer leaves later dims half-applied. 2D rigidbodies freeze during Unscaled-pause photo sessions like 3D ones. Touch: UI-blocked touch ids can't leak anymore (blocking stopped working or swallowed drags after repeated sessions), and two-finger pan speed is frame-rate independent. Restoring a replaced Input System module re-enables only the actions that were enabled before, and photo mode's own UI actions are disabled on exit. Layer exports keep double-sided geometry (no backface holes), fail cleanly when a layer shader is stripped, escape object names properly in the object-ID sidecar, and collision-suffixed files pair with their own sidecar and are handled by the gallery and delete. Photo file timestamps and the viewer caption use the invariant culture (non-Gregorian system calendars broke filename ordering). URP/HDRP curve editing no longer strands one native curve texture per channel per edit. Demo: campfire flames rise instead of streaming sideways, the flicker yields to photo-mode Scene Dim, toggle rows are clickable across the whole row, outlined text actually renders its outline, the orbit camera no longer consumes the exit-frame mouse delta, and critters can't overshoot waypoints on frame hitches. Editor: shot lists with a null grade/bookmark slot can't render mislabeled or mis-posed shots anymore; rebuilding demo assets on HDRP keeps the shipped LUT filters instead of silently overwriting them with no-ops; "Add Photo Mode To Scene" warns before adding a second controller; unticking the welcome window's "don't show again" is respected. Gallery "go to shot" lands exactly in Fly mode too: a pose beyond MaxDistance re-centers the roam pivot instead of snapping back to the sphere edge next frame. Render-layer exports use the beauty capture's GPU-limit-clamped supersample (no more mismatched or failed layers on 5K displays), and the photo's metadata records the factor actually used. HDRP depth/normal/motion-vector layer exports render at full float precision — the AOV buffers were 8-bit sRGB, which quantized depth to 256 levels and clamped negative motion vectors to zero. Layer exports skip ShadowsOnly shadow proxies and draw only each LODGroup's LOD0, instead of z-fighting every LOD…

Fixed ¶ Right panel no longer jumps toward a selected control when you click one - scroll-follow now runs only for keyboard/gamepad navigation, never for pointer presses. Capture Studio preview updates with grade changes on the Built-in fallback path in Edit Mode (the fallback post effect now runs outside Play Mode). Dragging a light's on-screen marker now keeps the marker under the cursor: the pointer is projected onto the light's orbit sphere instead of mapping raw pixel deltas to angles (whose screen direction flipped with the camera view, making markers orbit away from the mouse). A gallery Download button ("DOWNLOAD ALL" / "DOWNLOAD X IMAGES") downloads one image as PNG or several as a single zip (PhotoModePro_Captures_ .zip). Gallery: long-press (1 s) a thumbnail to multi-select; click toggles; Esc / CANCEL / unticking the last photo exits selection mode. Every delete (single, multi, viewer) is two-step: the first press arms the button as an inline confirmation with a visible 3.5 s countdown bar. Rebuilt around one thesis: HDRP-class and offline-renderer-class capture on every render pipeline, at runtime and in the editor. Added ¶ Runtime relight rig : up to six virtual lights (key / fill / rim / practical / sun) with photometric units (candela, lux, lumens), orbit and aim gizmos, light presets, scene-light tracking and a scene dimmer that scales lights, ambient and reflections with exact restore on exit. Rig setups save into bookmarks and player looks. Render-layer (AOV) export : every capture can additionally write depth (32-bit EXR), normals (16-bit EXR), albedo, per-object ID mattes with a name-to-color JSON sidecar, and a clean-alpha pass - on URP, HDRP and Built-in. Per-pass files by design (Unity's EXR encoder is single-part). Tiled capture : 8K/16K/32K output rendered as frustum-offset tiles and streamed scanline-by-scanline into one PNG - no gigapixel RenderTexture. Screen-space effects that would seam are suppressed with the reason shown; HDRP auto-exposure is metered and locked so tiles match. Physical camera : sensor presets, focal length, f-stop / shutter / ISO with EV coupling (grain follows ISO, motion blur follows shutter); drives HDRP's native physical camera where present. Editor Capture Studio : compose with bookmarks, run shot lists (bookmarks x grades x output presets), batch-capture headlessly in CI. Play-Mode-only on HDRP (Edit-Mode volumes do not apply to manual renders). Grade stack 7 -> 18 adjustments : bloom, chromatic aberration, lens distortion, tint, shadows/midtones/highlights color balance, RGB curves, HSL qualifier, tilt-shift, sharpen, motion blur - per-pipeline capability gated with reasons. LUT filters and looks : 24 built-in LUT filters, .cube import and export, player looks saved as portable JSON (adjustments + rig + dim). Gallery : in-game browsing with thumbnails, metadata sidecars and one-tap reframe-to-shot. Animation scrubbing while frozen, with exact restore. Composition aids : histogram, focus peaking, zebras, horizon level, composition guides. WebGL support : photos arrive as browser downloads; the gallery and looks persist in IndexedDB across reloads. Android touch support : one-finger look, pinch zoom, two-finger pan, larger touch targets and a responsive portrait layout. 2D / orthographic support : pan/zoom camera (FOV control becomes Zoom), sorting-layer hiding with exact restore; orbit and physical camera hide. Two new demo scenes (cinematic exterior, interior product set) plus a 2D demo scene built from generated sprites. Changed ¶ The scene-light dimmer now also scales ambient light, reflection intensity and solid-color camera backgrounds (on HDRP it scales lights only - the ambient term belongs to HDRP's sky/exposure system). Pixel-truth tests assert the rig visibly lights rendered surfaces and that dim/restore are exact. Known limitations ¶ Transparent capture remains unavailable on HDRP; PPv2 has no motion blur or RGB curves; Capture Studio is Play-Mode-only on HDRP; iOS untested (roadmap); consoles untested.

Added ¶ Setup Wizard (Tools → Photo Mode Pro → Setup Wizard): green/yellow/red project checks — render pipeline, effects backend, input handling, Cinemachine, TextMesh Pro essentials, demo materials — with one-click fixes where automatable, and an Add Photo Mode To Scene button that drops the configured prefab into the open scene and selects it. Editor menu root Tools → Photo Mode Pro: Setup Wizard, Add Photo Mode To Scene, Run Self-Test, Build Demo Assets, Open Documentation, Report a Bug (pre-filled email), Welcome and About (version + latest changelog). First-import welcome window , shown once per machine (EditorPrefs-gated with a version-independent key — package updates never re-show it; never in batch mode), linking the wizard, documentation and support. Pipeline-aware demo : demo materials are generated for the ACTIVE render pipeline (Standard / URP Lit / HDRP Lit), so the demo is never pink. Opening the demo scene under a mismatched pipeline offers "Rebuild demo for current pipeline" (persisted don't ask again ; never in batch mode); the wizard offers the same fix. Self-test utility (Tools → Photo Mode Pro → Run Self-Test, or -executeMethod PhotoModePro.Editor.PhotoModeSelfTest.Run ): verifies compilation, runs the wizard checks headlessly, rebuilds the demo and validates the generated materials, writing a JSON result file. Documentation site at https://danmaxpublishing.github.io/docs/ (quick start, how-tos, integrations, per-pipeline notes, FAQ, troubleshooting, API reference) plus an offline quick start in the package root. Fixed ¶ Aperture slider dead zone : the slider was linear in f-stops while depth-of-field blur scales with 1/f-number, so everything visible happened below ~f/3. The slider now spans f/0.7–f/16 on a perceptual log-stop mapping (equal travel = equal stop ratio) and the full travel produces visible change. Out-of-range aperture values from presets or scripts (the old range reached f/32) are clamped when applied — the property still accepts any positive value, no API break. Hotkey hint chips relayout : the four stacked rows in the bottom-left corner are replaced by a single centered row of chips along the bottom screen edge (the toolbar moved up to clear it). On canvases too narrow for one row (narrower than ~1.15:1) trailing chips wrap onto a second row stacked above. Chip metrics are unchanged. Focus rings clipped again on wide controls (regression of an earlier fix): the existing padding was still present but did not account for the hover/selection scale-up the button feedback applies — on full-width controls the scaled ring crossed the scroll-view mask. Page padding is now computed from the selection-scale invariant, and a geometry regression test proves every ring stays inside the mask at selection scale on the generated prefab. Fixed (QA pass) ¶ A pre-existing EventSystem gets its original UI actions back on exit — the D-pad-only navigation scheme photo mode applies no longer persists into the game's own menus. Disabling or destroying the controller mid-capture no longer wedges photo mode open (time scale, cursor, audio, camera and spawned objects are all released; the abandoned capture frees its RenderTexture and textures). Effects backends destroy the volume components they created on exit; long sessions no longer strand a handful of ScriptableObjects per enter/exit cycle. HDRP on Unity 2021.3/2022.1 (HDRP 12/13) compiles again: the photo camera's aperture goes through HDPhysicalCamera there, and the HDRP-14-only focusDistanceMode override is version-guarded (same behavior on all versions). The PPv2 backend's template-layer lookup no longer requires 2021.3.18+. Photo file names are sanitized with a platform-independent character set, so captures named on macOS/Linux stay portable to Windows. The capture thumbnail no longer leaks in UI-less (pure API) integrations, and its ownership is documented on OnPhotoCaptured . Added ¶ Unity 2021.3+ support. The minimum Unity version drops from 6000.0 to 2021.3 LTS; the package is verified on 2021.3, 2022.3 and 6000.3, on URP 12/14/17, Built-in (PPv2 and fallback) and HDRP, with the new Input System, the legacy Input Manager and Active Input Handling = Both. PhotoModeSettings.AudioPauseMode ( AudioPauseMode.AudioListenerPause / AudioPauseMode.None ): with None the package never touches audio, so mixer-snapshot-based games can drive their own transitions from the enter/exit events. Migration note: this replaces the pauseAudio bool; projects that had unchecked pauseAudio must select None once on their settings asset. PhotoModeController.ExitedThisFrame : true only during the frame photo mode closed. Gameplay code sharing bindings with photo mode (e.g. Space as jump and fly-up) skips input that frame so the closing press cannot bleed through; the demo character uses the pattern and QuickStart documents it. Missing-EventSystem handling: if the scene has no EventSystem when the UI opens, photo mode creates one (matching the active input handling), logs a single info message and removes it on exit — the scene is left exactly as found. Scene-change safety: loading or unloading a scene while photo mode is open now auto-closes it cleanly (time scale, audio, cursor, visibility restored first; an in-flight capture is abandoned), with an OnDestroy safety net if the controller itself is torn down. PhotoModeUIController.EnsureSelection() : selects the first control of the active category when nothing is selected (used by the new navigation fallback, available to integrators). IL2CPP build proof: a smoke-test player (IL2CPP, Managed Stripping Level = High) opens photo mode, applies a preset, captures at 2x and verifies the PNG — run as part of the release checks. Fixed ¶ Arrow/D-pad navigation is live the moment photo mode opens: the first control of the active tab is auto-selected (focus ring visible), and pressing a navigation key while nothing is selected (e.g. after a mouse click) selects it again — navigation can never go dead. The side panel scroll view now follows keyboard/gamepad selection with minimal auto-scroll: it moves just enough to reveal the selected control plus its focus ring and never moves when the selection is already visible. Focus rings are no longer clipped by the scroll-view mask: pages pad their content (8 px) so rings fit fully inside the viewport on all sides (toggles, preset buttons, Fly/Orbit, 1x/2x/4x, capture-folder row). The NONE preset button is gone: Clean is now the first preset and the active default (the current-preset label reads "Clean" on open and after any reset). ApplyPreset(null) remains the programmatic reset and maps to the same state — no API break. Hotkey hint chips (photo mode bar and demo HUD) scaled ×1.5 (font 11 → 16.5) for readability; the photo-mode bar regroups into four short rows so nothing collides with the toolbar at 21:9, 16:9 or 4:3. Hide Player now disables the player's Renderer components instead of deactivating the GameObject, so CharacterController/Animator/physics state survives hide → unhide → exit with zero pops or jumps (regression-tested for exact position/velocity/grounded equality). The D-pad UI actions asset is built once and reused; repeated open/close no longer accumulates ScriptableObjects. Slider value labels use cached label lookups and TextMeshPro's non-allocating numeric SetText , making slider drags GC-free. Performance ¶ Zero per-frame GC allocations while photo mode is open and idle and while adjusting sliders; the idle paths are asserted by allocation gates in the release test suite. No per-frame work besides the toggle poll while closed.

Fixed ¶ All side-panel pages now live in a shared ScrollRect with a slim scrollbar; the mouse wheel scrolls the panel when the pointer is over UI and zooms the camera otherwise. The expanding soft-glow control highlight is replaced by a thin (~2 px) snug outline ring — circular on slider knobs and toggles, rounded-rect on buttons and tabs — that never overlaps neighboring controls or hides the toggle checkmark. Mouse clicks clear the EventSystem selection, so the focus ring appears only during keyboard/gamepad navigation (and sliders now show it). Wheel zoom updates the FOV slider and readout live (two-way sync; roll too). The FOV slider range follows PhotoModeSettings.MinFov/MaxFov instead of the hardcoded 10–120. The Focus Dist slider uses a logarithmic mapping over 0.1–100 m (half the travel covers the visibly-focus-pulling 0.1–3 m); the readout stays in meters. Focus Dist and Aperture rows hide while Depth of Field is off. HDRP: Focus Dist and Aperture sliders now work — FOV smoothing was silently resetting the physical camera every frame ( fieldOfView writes); the camera is now driven via focalLength while physical properties are in use. Capture feedback (white flash, shutter sound, thumbnail toast) is exempt from Hide UI on every pipeline: the root canvas stays enabled and only the chrome (toolbar, panel, hint bar) hides. 2x/4x captures show a static "Processing…" badge for the duration of the blocking render; the badge never appears in the captured photo. Film grain response is normalized across pipelines (URP boosted toward the PPv2 look) and PPv2 vignette response is boosted toward the URP look. The demo character no longer scale-pops when jumping or after Hide Player: the animator now uses de-scaled copies of the imported clips. Sprint (Shift) now multiplies Z/C roll speed by the same SprintMultiplier as movement. Added ¶ Clickable capture toast: opens the file browser with the new photo selected (Windows Explorer reveal; folder open elsewhere). The save-path row on the CAPTURE tab is clickable too and opens the capture folder. Hint bar chips for "Space/Ctrl · Up/Down" and "Z/C · Roll" (7 chips total). Scene-floating text (hint labels, toolbar Q/E hints, toast filename) gets a thin black TMP outline + underlay for readability over bright surfaces. The demo HUD is rebuilt from the photo-mode UI building blocks (TMP text, rounded keycap chips, theme colors). Changing a hotkey on the settings asset offers to update the matching UI prefab hint chips (editor dialog).

Added ¶ Built-in Render Pipeline support : a Post Processing Stack v2 backend (own PostProcessVolume + profile + layer on the photo camera, full adjustment set) when com.unity.postprocessing is installed, and a minimal fallback backend (exposure / contrast / saturation / vignette via one internal full-screen shader) when it is not. HDRP support : an HDRP volume backend (ColorAdjustments, WhiteBalance, Vignette, FilmGrain, DepthOfField) using the physical camera for depth of field (aperture drives Camera.aperture ). Exposure maps to ColorAdjustments.postExposure — relative EV, same semantics as URP. Capability system : EffectCapabilities flags ( PhotoModePro.Effects ), reported per backend via the new IPhotoModeEffectsBackend.Capabilities property and surfaced through PhotoModeController.ActiveCapabilities (live prediction while photo mode is inactive). The runtime UI hides controls — and whole categories — for unsupported effects; gamepad navigation never lands on a dead control. Backend selection : automatic detection from the active render pipeline asset, with a manual PhotoModeSettings.BackendOverride ( Auto / Urp / Hdrp / PostProcessingV2 / BuiltInFallback ). An unavailable forced backend logs one warning and falls back to Auto. package.json ( com.danmax.photomodepro ) so the asset folder can be consumed as a local UPM package; PipelineTestSceneBuilder editor bootstrap that builds a minimal pipeline-appropriate test scene in any host project. Capture path audit: temporal anti-aliasing (URP and HDRP) is disabled for the duration of every capture and dynamic resolution is forced off, so 1x/2x/4x supersampled output is artifact-free and exactly the requested size. Changed ¶ Breaking for custom backend implementors : IPhotoModeEffectsBackend gains EffectCapabilities Capabilities { get; } and Initialize() is now Initialize(Camera photoCamera) . Backends that ignore the camera can simply discard the argument. Transparent capture is clamped at the backend boundary: the request is ignored when the active backend cannot produce clean alpha (HDRP). On both Built-in variants transparent capture disables the system's PPv2 volume/layer or skips the fallback blit for the shot, matching URP semantics. Known limitations ¶ HDRP reports TransparentCapture as unsupported (clean alpha would require an alpha-capable color buffer format on the HDRP asset, which the package does not edit). The Built-in fallback backend (no PPv2) supports exposure, contrast, saturation and vignette only; temperature, film grain and depth of field controls are hidden.

Added ¶ Demo upgrade: the primitive corridor is replaced by a stylized forest-clearing showcase scene (CC0 third-party assets, provenance in Demo/ThirdParty/ATTRIBUTIONS.md ), still built 100% programmatically by DemoSceneBuilder . Rigged, animated low-poly adventurer with a from-scratch third-person controller ( ThirdPersonCharacter ): camera-relative WASD / left-stick movement, walk/run sprint, smooth acceleration, gravity and jump; freezes cleanly while photo mode is active. Third-person follow camera ( ThirdPersonFollowCamera ) with mouse / right-stick orbit, clamped pitch, smoothed follow and sphere-cast collision; hands off to and restores from the photo mode free camera. 2K golden-hour HDRI skybox with matched directional sun, URP fog and atmosphere tuned for the DoF / filter presets. Campfire hero prop: scripted flickering point light ( CampfireFlicker ), code-built fire and smoke particles, drifting fireflies and dust motes. Ambient forest audio plus positional campfire crackle — audibly paused by photo mode's AudioListener.pause showcase. Wandering ambient critters on scripted waypoint patrols ( CritterPatrol ). Physics props (crates/barrels) the character can bump around. Deterministic seeded scatter for trees/rocks/grass ( DemoScatterMath ), code-generated forest-floor mesh and code-built animator controllers. Removed ¶ SimplePlayerMovement (superseded by ThirdPersonCharacter ).

Added ¶ Photo mode controller with EnterPhotoMode() / ExitPhotoMode() public API, static PhotoModeController.Instance accessor, C# events and UnityEvent mirrors ( OnEntered , OnExited , OnPhotoCaptured(path, thumbnail) ). DemoSceneBuilder editor tool that programmatically generates the demo scene, UI prefab, controller prefab, settings, theme and preset assets. EditMode and PlayMode test suites (Unity Test Framework).

How to move an existing project to a newer Photo Mode Pro version, newest first. Each step lists what changed, who is affected, and what (if anything) you must do. The full change list lives in the Changelog . After any upgrade Let Unity reimport the package fully. Run Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Run Self-Test . It writes PhotoModeSelfTest.json and verifies your setup end to end. If you ship a modified copy of the demo, rebuild it via Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Build Demo Assets .

No breaking API changes and no action required. Two behavioral changes to be aware of: Scene Dim also dims ambient light and backgrounds ¶ The relighting panel's Scene Dim now scales the ambient/reflection environment and solid-color camera backgrounds along with the scene's lights (previously only the lights dimmed, so outdoor scenes stayed bright and rig lights could not read through). Everything is still restored exactly on exit. Only act if you tuned screenshots against the old lights-only behavior: re-check your dim percentage. WebGL captures save to the Gallery instead of downloading ¶ On WebGL, captures no longer trigger a browser download per photo; they save to the in-game Gallery (persisted in IndexedDB), and the Gallery's DOWNLOAD button exports one PNG or a zip of several. If your players relied on the per-capture download prompt, point them at the Gallery button.

No breaking API changes. Two behavioral changes and new editor tooling: Aperture range and mapping ¶ The aperture constants changed: APERTURE_MIN / APERTURE_MAX are now 0.7/16 (previously 1/32), and the slider uses a perceptual log-stop mapping so its full travel produces visible depth-of-field change. The aperture property still accepts any positive value; out-of-range values from old presets, saved settings or scripts clamp into f/0.7–f/16 when applied . Presets you re-save automatically clamp to the new range. Only act if your code or presets relied on apertures outside f/0.7–f/16: values below 0.7 now behave as f/0.7 and values above 16 as f/16. UI layout: hint chips and toolbar ¶ Hotkey hint chips now form a single row along the bottom screen edge (wrapping to a second row only on very narrow/portrait windows), and the toolbar is raised so the two bands cannot intersect. No action if you use the generated UI prefab as shipped; it updates with the package. If you modified the generated UI prefab , regenerate it ( Tools > Photo Mode Pro > Build Demo Assets ) and re-apply your customizations, or merge the layout changes manually. New editor menus ¶ Everything now lives under Tools > Photo Mode Pro : Setup Wizard, Add Photo Mode To Scene, Run Self-Test, Build Demo Assets, Open Documentation, Report a Bug, Welcome, and About. The Setup Wizard runs green/yellow/red checks (pipeline, effects backend, input handling, Cinemachine, TMP essentials, demo materials) with one-click fixes. Run it once after upgrading. The demo is also pipeline-aware now (no longer URP-only): opening the demo scene under a mismatched pipeline offers a one-click rebuild. A first-import Welcome window appears once per machine and is never re-shown across updates.

pauseAudio replaced by AudioPauseMode ¶ The pauseAudio bool on PhotoModeSettings was replaced by the AudioPauseMode enum ( AudioPauseMode.AudioListenerPause / AudioPauseMode.None ). Old serialized assets fall back to the default, AudioListenerPause (the same behavior as the old pauseAudio = true ). No action for most projects. Action required if you had unchecked pauseAudio : select AudioPauseMode.None once on your settings asset. With None the package never touches audio, so drive your own mixer-snapshot transitions from OnEntered / OnExited ; see Events and API . NONE preset button removed ¶ Clean is now the first preset and the active default; the NONE button is gone because it was indistinguishable from Clean. ApplyPreset(null) still works as the programmatic reset and maps to the same state: no API break . See Presets . Minimum Unity version drops to 2021.3 ¶ 0.9.0 lowers the minimum from Unity 6000.0 to 2021.3 LTS (verified on 2021.3, 2022.3 and 6000.3, across URP/HDRP/Built-in and both input handlers). Purely additive; nothing to migrate. See the Support Matrix .

Breaking: IPhotoModeEffectsBackend (custom backend implementors only) ¶ If you implemented your own effects backend, two interface changes apply: public interface IPhotoModeEffectsBackend { // New in 0.8.0: report what your backend can do. EffectCapabilities Capabilities { get ; } // Changed in 0.8.0: Initialize() now receives the photo camera. void Initialize ( Camera photoCamera ); // ...unchanged members... } Add the Capabilities property (return the EffectCapabilities flags your backend supports; the UI hides controls for everything else). Update Initialize() to Initialize(Camera photoCamera) ; backends that do not need the camera can simply discard the argument. Projects that only use the built-in backends are unaffected. Backend selection is automatic, with a manual PhotoModeSettings.BackendOverride if you need to force one. See Effects and Pipelines .

Apply the steps above in order (0.8.0 → 0.9.0 → 1.0.0 → 1.1.x). In practice, unless you wrote a custom effects backend or unchecked pauseAudio , upgrading is: import, reimport, run the Self-Test, and rebuild the demo if you modified it. If anything misbehaves afterwards, start with Troubleshooting .
